lines.en: After the Demon King Selection ended, the ‘Yoo Joonghyuk―Kim Dokja Industrial Complex’ became busy with reconstruction.

The citizens faced the prospect of homelessness in the aftermath of the war, and their faces were bleak. If not for the relief supplies I had persuaded Bihyung to provide, the mood would have been even uglier.
“The clock tower goes over there! Hey, watch out!”

With the dukes dead, citizens from other industrial complexes arrived in an endless stream, so there was no shortage of labor. I spent two days helping the citizens rebuild, and the city was gradually regaining its vitality.
“Thank you for helping, Yoo Sangah-ssi.”
Without Yoo Sangah’s [Arachne’s Web], the initial reconstruction would have taken much longer. Wiping the sweat from her forehead, Yoo Sangah said,
“……You should get some rest too, Dokja-ssi.”
“I’m fine. How about you, Yoo Sangah-ssi?”
Yoo Sangah studied the bandages wrapped around my chest before answering.
“I’m in good condition too.”
Good condition……
Somehow, that choice of words was very like Yoo Sangah.
I stopped working and climbed the clock tower with Yoo Sangah to look down over the square.

Yoo Joonghyuk and the other seriously injured members of our group were hospitalized in Aileen’s ward. Jung Heewon and Lee Jihye, whose injuries had been relatively minor, were helping with construction near the entrance to the complex. From the ward, I could hear Lee Hyunsung stubbornly insisting that he was all better and would be checking out.
Perhaps thanks to two days of hard work, at least the area around the square was beginning to look like a place people lived.
The schedule was tight, but pushing ourselves now would pay off later.
“Here they come.”
A portal shimmering in midair.
A little kid was racing toward us from the square at incredible speed.
I lightly jumped down from the clock tower to greet him.
“Dokja hyung! Waaaaaaah!”
Lee Gilyoung threw himself into my arms and squirmed against me. I smiled and ruffled his hair.
“Been doing well? Looks like you’ve grown a little.”
“Really?”
“Yeah. You must be almost as tall as Yoosung now.”
“I’ll be taller soon!”
Lee Gilyoung wasn’t the only one who had come through the portal in midair. A large man landed in the square with a thud.
“It’s been a while, Gong Pildu-ssi.”
“……Hmph.”

As though he had no interest whatsoever in my well-being, Gong Pildu glared at me briefly before giving Yoo Sangah a small wave. When she bowed her head with a faint smile, his mood seemed to improve a little.
“I didn’t come to see you, you bastard.”
Still, even this showed how much Gong Pildu had changed.
Who could call him one of the Ten Evils now?
“Where’s Han Sooyoung?”
“Sooyoung noona said she thinks she’ll need to recuperate for a while.”
Lee Gilyoung spoke as he lightly bumped his forehead against my stomach.
Recuperate……
Even if she had offered up [Abyss Stones], having the Black Flame Dragon descend into her body while bearing the probability cost must have taken a considerable toll.
But surely it couldn’t be bad enough to keep her from coming here……
“Oh, Sooyoung noona told me to give you this.”
Lee Gilyoung rummaged through his pocket and handed me a note.
True to Han Sooyoung, it had been folded over and over with an oddly obsessive persistence.
Shielding it from Lee Gilyoung’s sparkling eyes, I carefully opened the note.
―Make me do this shit again and I’ll kill you.
A chuckle escaped me.
Just as I thought. She had a reason for not coming.
Even now, closing my eyes brought back the image of Han Sooyoung wrapped in bandages and rampaging like a crazy bitch.
―There are still a few problems left.

The note contained some other information as well. Things you could only hear about on Earth, such as the situation on the Korean Peninsula and relations between nebulae. Fortunately, Earth didn’t seem to have strayed far from the cycle of events in the original novel I knew. In fact, I already knew most of it, so there was no need for her to pass it along like this.
Perhaps Han Sooyoung knew that too, because she kept rambling and repeating herself.
―Anyway, that’s how it is…… Well…… Take care, idiot. See you when you get to Earth.
What a shame. I’d been planning to really tease her when we met this time.
I put the note inside my coat and addressed Lee Gilyoung and Gong Pildu.
“There will be a banquet tonight. Go inside, wash up, and get ready.”
“A banquet?”
“We’re expecting some guests.”
We had made it through one crisis for now.
But this industrial complex’s troubles were only just beginning.
[The constellation ‘God of Wine and Ecstasy’ accepts your invitation.]
[The constellation ‘Queen of the Darkest Spring’ accepts your invitation.]
Watching the countless indirect messages pouring out of the air, I let out a small sigh.
Yoo Joonghyuk still hadn’t woken up since the selection.
“How much longer will it take him to recover?”
“He’ll need at least another 2 weeks.”
After checking Yoo Joonghyuk’s pulse, Aileen glanced at me on her way out of the room.
“……And you need some rest too. You know that, right?”
“Don’t worry.”
Even after Aileen left, I stayed in Yoo Joonghyuk’s room.

His sleeping face was paler than that of any ‘Yoo Joonghyuk’ I had ever seen. Naturally. This was the first Yoo Joonghyuk who hadn’t gone back despite suffering injuries serious enough to activate ‘Regression.’
I stood up and checked the Story packs connected to him.
Hooking up the wrong Story pack could even cause fatal side effects from having to endure the cringe (降魔).
It was a little different if you had [Lamarck’s Giraffe], like me……
“……Even the packs he uses are just like him.”
「Here I Come, You Lonely World」
「Becoming a Sword Master Was the Easiest Part」
「I’ve Wielded a Sword Since I Was Five—I Was a Genius」

Fortunately, Aileen, a Story Expert, seemed to have a good grasp of Yoo Joonghyuk’s Story composition. In fact, the Yoo Joonghyuk of the 144th round had once briefly gone mad after mistakenly receiving a transfusion of Lee Hyunsung’s military Story.
“He’s a picky eater.”
The voice that suddenly came from behind me startled me so badly that I nearly had a fit.
When I turned, a beautiful giant was leaning against the wall.
“……How long have you been there?”
“Since before you came in.”
The Breaking the Sky Sword Saint looked down at me calmly, then glanced at Yoo Joonghyuk.
“This treatment is excessive. Toss him a few Murim dumplings and he’d be better in no time.”
“We don’t have any Murim dumplings here.”
Despite her words, the look in the Breaking the Sky Sword Saint’s eyes was exceedingly gentle.
That was when a fearsome man’s voice rang out.
“So, is that the bastard who hit you?”
Something the size of a frog was clinging upside down to the ceiling opposite the Breaking the Sky Sword Saint.
It was Kyrgios Rodgraim.
“Master.”
“Tell me. Was it him?”

Come to think of it, I remembered the nonsense I’d spouted when I sent Kyrgios to Murim. Hadn’t I said the Breaking the Sky Sword Saint’s disciple had beaten me up? Kyrgios’s handsome brows curved, and the aura of [Electrification] began to envelop his entire body.
“Was it all a lie?”
I swallowed and scrambled for something to say.
“Well, it wasn’t entirely a lie! We’re actually on pretty bad terms. He really has beaten me up before……”
“Were you only on the receiving end?”
“Of course, I’ve hit him too……”

Though I had exploited a loophole in the system, I had beaten Yoo Joonghyuk to a bloody pulp during the struggle for the throne, so it wasn’t a lie. A flicker of interest crossed the Breaking the Sky Sword Saint’s face as she listened.
“Hmm. You hit my disciple?”
“So who won?”
The two masters’ gazes clashed in midair.
Their eyes had merely met, yet my perception of space warped and sparks began to fly.
Since the two had come back together, I’d assumed their relationship must have improved. Apparently, that had been wishful thinking. The Breaking the Sky Sword Saint spoke in an icy voice.
“What a foolish question. One look at their faces makes it obvious that my disciple is a cut above yours.”
“My disciple could never be weaker than a pretty boy who’s done nothing but build muscle. He may not look it, but I’ve passed down my secret martial art to him……”
“And I’m sure it’s just another martial art that makes you smaller.”
Bzzzzzzzt!
At this rate, the hospital room looked likely to explode, so I quickly stepped between them.
“There’s something I’d like to ask you both.”
Two terrifying gazes fell on me at once. I activated my ‘Status’ and barely withstood the pressure as I asked,
“What happened to <First Murim>?”
It was a question I’d been wondering about all along.
Since the Breaking the Sky Sword Saint and Kyrgios had come here, I knew Murim was probably safe. Still, their opponent had been an ‘Outer God.’
Kyrgios was the first to speak.
“Hmph. I went there in person. Do you think I couldn’t save a single world like that?”
With that, Kyrgios flew straight out the window, as though something had offended him.
……What was his problem?
The Breaking the Sky Sword Saint quietly watched the window Kyrgios had flown through before speaking.
“We did stop it, but it’s hard to say we stopped everything.”
“Did you defeat the ‘Outer God’?”
The faint presence of a ‘Giant Story’ emanating from the Breaking the Sky Sword Saint’s entire body.
It was probably a Giant Story connected to <First Murim>. It had to be.
The Breaking the Sky Sword Saint gave a slight nod.
“It was a formidable opponent, but not beyond us. That obnoxious Paradox bastard came to help, after all.”
Only someone on the Breaking the Sky Sword Saint’s level could describe an Outer God as merely a ‘formidable opponent.’
“The problem was the one that came after it.”
Even Outer Gods had ranks.
In other words, there were named ones among them too.
For example, the gods collectively known as ‘Old Ones’ or ‘Great Old Ones.’
―It was neither an ‘Old One’ nor a ‘Great Old One.’
But among them were unfathomable beings that transcended even those categories.

―I’d never seen anything like it, so I can’t give you a clear explanation of what it was. What I can say for certain is that even Paradox and I together were no match for it. In fact, it wasn’t even a fight. If it hadn’t withdrawn of its own accord, we would have vanished from the universe along with Murim.
The Breaking the Sky Sword Saint’s words sounded downright strange.

According to the original novel’s events, there was absolutely no probability that would allow a god like that to appear in <First Murim> that day. Yet such an immense god had appeared, then withdrawn just as inexplicably.
―It vanished as though it had found some other delicious prey.
A being that was neither an Old One nor a Great Old One.
A god so powerful that merely looking at it made mighty figures like the Breaking the Sky Sword Saint and the White Snow of Pitch freeze and lose the will to fight……
Waaaaaah!
A modest party was underway in the [Industrial Complex]’s central hall. Some of my companions had recovered. I could also see the symbolic bodies of several invited constellations.
[Hmm, Demon King of Salvation. Did you receive the gift I sent?]

Persephone approached with a mischievous smile. As expected, her symbolic body looked like Yoo Sangah again. My companions, seeing her symbolic body for the first time, looked startled. Yoo Sangah’s expression in particular was quite a sight.
“……I don’t like garter belts anymore.”
Dressed in a cheongsam, Persephone laughed and waved her fan.
[Really? I sent one with quite good performance.]
At the word ‘performance,’ I saw Lee Hyunsung perk up beside me.
I quickly spoke before he could say anything outlandish.
“I’m indebted to you for your help during the selection.”
[Hmm, but I didn’t do anything.]
“I know you persuaded the ‘Master of the Skywalk.’”
<Olympus> was currently divided. If she hadn’t persuaded Hermes, I might have had to fight even more constellations from <Olympus> during the selection.
[Think of it as an investment in the future.]

With a faint smile, Persephone went to the center of the hall and began to dance, apparently in a good mood. She even pulled Yoo Sangah in to be her partner. Though flustered at first, Yoo Sangah soon maintained a cool expression, as if determined not to lose. Jung Heewon whistled.
“Looking good, Sangah-ssi!”

Dionysus had already finished his tenth toast in a corner. I also saw Cheok Jungyeong sharing drinks with the ‘Hasty Swamp Judge.’ Though it was a small banquet, the sight put me more at ease than any banquet I had attended before.
[A rare moment of rest. Congratulations, Demon King of Salvation.]
I turned to find an old man standing there in an elegant suit.
“You’ve arrived, Mass Production Maker.”
He, too, was one of the constellations who had helped in this ‘selection.’
[I enjoyed your Story. You certainly had reason to talk big at the Gourmet Association.]
“You flatter me.”
I picked up a glass from the table and clinked glasses with the ‘Mass Production Maker.’
The smell told me it was quite strong, so I merely touched it to my lips and set it back down.
Neither of us spoke for a moment.
The ‘Mass Production Maker’ was probably choosing his question.
And that question was precisely why he and the other constellations were here—and why I had held this banquet.
The ‘Mass Production Maker’ took a sip and spoke as if in passing.
[Now that you’ve obtained the ‘Qualification for the End,’ I suppose the filtering has been lifted.]
I felt a subtle change in the atmosphere.
I nodded and replied,
“It has.”

The hall was still boisterous, but one by one, the constellations’ eyes turned toward me. Persephone, Cheok Jungyeong, Dionysus…… In truth, they had all been listening to our conversation while pretending to be uninterested.
Once every constellation’s gaze was fixed on me, the ‘Mass Production Maker’ asked,
[May I ask what your ■■ was?]
What was my ■■?
I had naturally expected that question from the ‘Mass Production Maker.’
“Are you curious?”
[Is there anyone here who isn’t?]

As the Mass Production Maker smiled faintly, several constellations cleared their throats. Sensing the unusual turn in the atmosphere, my other companions, who still didn’t understand what was happening, began to focus on me too.
“Why is everyone suddenly……”
“Shh.”
Jung Heewon stopped Lee Hyunsung from cluelessly interrupting.
I slowly looked around at everyone present. Before I knew it, every being in the hall was watching me.
In ‘Ways of Survival,’ it went by a great many names.
For example, the ‘King of the Dokkaebis’ had said this:
「The end and beginning of every story.」
But Yoo Joonghyuk would say this:
「The goddamn Star Stream.」

Lee Hyunsung would call it “discharge from the military,” and Yoo Sangah might call it “retirement planning.” For Lee Jihye, it would be “graduation.” And surprisingly, none of those interpretations of ■■ would be wrong.
The Mass Production Maker asked,
[Everyone who obtains the ‘Qualification for the End’ receives a different name for their ‘end.’ Did you know that?]
“Since everyone possesses different Stories, I suppose that’s only natural.”

■■ had never been a proper noun whose exact meaning could be communicated. The filtering being lifted simply meant I could now ‘read’ it. The other constellations who had received a hidden scenario like mine were probably all in a similar position.
<Hidden Scenario ― A Single Story>
Category: Hidden
Difficulty: ???
Clear Conditions: Complete a single Story that will reach ■■.
Time Limit: ―
Reward: ???
Failure: ???
●At present, you have completed ‘Introduction (起).’
●For details, refer to the additional scenario description.
The hidden scenario, ‘A Single Story.’
This scenario was assigned to every being who obtained the ‘Qualification for the End.’
To search a sea of countless Stories in the vast galaxy of the <Star Stream> and complete a single ‘perfect story.’
Legendary-grade Stories, Myth-grade Stories, and even the Giant Story I had obtained were ultimately only steps on the journey toward that ‘single story.’
The Mass Production Maker in front of me and Persephone over there would have received this scenario too. Of course, the places they ultimately reached would be different from mine.
[Baat!]
Before I could even tell her, Biyoo cut off the channel in the hall.
She had probably sensed instinctively that what we were about to discuss was important.
As protesting messages from constellations flowed out of the air, the ‘Mass Production Maker’ spoke in a solemn tone.
[My ■■ was ‘Exhaustion (枯渴).’]
I was a little surprised, not having expected him to reveal his hand so readily.
Then Persephone, who had been dancing on the stage, spoke as well.
[Mine was ‘Death.’]
Exhaustion and Death.
Both were words that could symbolize the ‘end’ of something.
They were also deeply paradoxical ends for the ‘Mass Production Maker,’ who always loved to make things, and ‘Persephone,’ who ruled the Underworld of the dead.
Now that they had shown their cards, I had nowhere left to retreat.
“Everyone, please swear on your modifiers that you won’t reveal what you hear from me here to anyone.”
Several constellations looked at one another at my words.
[Well, of course……]
[Ahem, is that really necessary? As if we’d go around telling anyone……]
[Just how extraordinary is your ■■ for you to keep us in such suspense?]
I didn’t answer immediately. I merely smiled.
A quiet ripple began to spread among the constellations.
[Could it be……?]
It felt as though I could see the thoughts flashing through their minds.
Watching their expressions, I thought,
Yes, think.
Ponder it. Question it.
Only then would the outcome I wanted take shape.
At last, when the constellations’ murmuring reached its peak, I slowly began to speak.
Han Sooyoung was walking down a street.
The landscape of Seoul lay in ruins. She was walking alone through streets without a single survivor.
All kinds of wild thoughts flitted through her mind.
Why am I here right now?
I was definitely fighting the constellations with Flame Dragon.
No, more importantly, ‘Seoul’ was supposed to be sealed off, so why……
―Flame Dragon?
The ‘Abyssal Black Flame Dragon’ didn’t answer.
―Hey, is anyone there?

Han Sooyoung shouted as she walked among collapsed multi-tenant buildings. Monster corpses lay strewn among the familiar ruined buildings of Gwanghwamun. Every time she passed one of the reeking corpses, goosebumps rose on her skin.
Every single one was a monster far beyond her current ability to handle.
What the hell. What happened?
She could ask, but there was no one to answer.
No, even if there were, perhaps it would be better if they didn’t answer.
If any ‘being’ remained alive here, it would be the terrifying monster that had reduced all those creatures to bloody pulp.
If this was a dream, she could only pray to wake up……
That was when something like a person’s shadow flashed past in the distance.
A familiar human figure (人形) in a white, pure-white coat.
Her heart swelled.
―Kim Dokja!
The moment the man turned toward her.
With the sound of flesh being pierced, a blade suddenly burst through his coat.
The white coat staining red.
Han Sooyoung woke with a scream.
“Hah, hah……”
Only after she blinked several times did her sense of reality slowly return.
“What the……”
Uncharacteristically, she even spoke to herself.
Her back was drenched in cold sweat.
[The constellation ‘Abyssal Black Flame Dragon’ is pleased that you are talking to yourself.]
[The constellation ‘Abyssal Black Flame Dragon,’ that you have finally become his true successor……]
“Shut up.”
With the Black Flame Dragon spouting nonsense, this certainly seemed to be reality.
Han Sooyoung pressed one hand to her temple.
……Why had he appeared in her dream?

Normally, Han Sooyoung would have dismissed it as a meaningless dream. But in a world where superstitions became reality, she couldn’t simply brush off even a dream like this. A moment later, she realized that the arm she had raised to her temple was wrapped in bandages.
“Goddammit. I still haven’t taken these off.”
“Leave them on. They’re there because you’re hurt.”
Startled, she turned to find a woman she knew standing there.
“……Kim Dokja’s mom?”
“You’re the only one who still calls me that.”
Lee Sookyung wiped Han Sooyoung’s back and forehead with a towel.
Han Sooyoung asked,
“Why didn’t you go to the Demon Realm?”
“How could I show my face there?”
“Kim Dokja would’ve liked it.”
“He would have liked it more if you’d gone.”
“……You don’t know your own son very well, ajumma.”

Han Sooyoung spoke with a slight pout. Lee Sookyung smiled faintly and replaced the damp pillowcase with a fresh one. Apparently liking the new pillowcase, Han Sooyoung buried her nose in it and sniffed before speaking.
“Still, it looks like things worked out somehow.”
“What do you mean?”
“Kim Dokja’s Great Misfortune (大凶) incident.”

Judging by how excited the Black Flame Dragon was, things seemed to have gone well in the Demon Realm too. The damage to the Korean Peninsula wasn’t as extensive as she’d expected. The Gyeonggi region had taken a hit, but they’d managed to evacuate the citizens safely……
That unsettling dream bothered her a little, but a dream was only a dream, after all……
“It isn’t all over.”

Without a word, Lee Sookyung brought over a dish and began to conjure a divination from [Good or Bad Luck, Disaster or Happiness Fortune] above it. Han Sooyoung silently read the trails of letters appearing over the water. She couldn’t believe it. So she asked Lee Sookyung to cast the divination again, over and over. The result was the same. Looking down at her heavily bandaged arm, Han Sooyoung said,
“Get in touch with Kim Dokja.”
That night, after the banquet. I was sitting alone in my office.
Normally, this would have been the perfect time to make a cup of hot chocolate and leisurely read ‘Ways of Survival,’ but I couldn’t afford that luxury now.
I was staring at a huge fragment on the table. It was a piece that had broken off the last car of the train where Surya and I had fought.
I closed my eyes and reconstructed my memories of that moment.
Surya’s train had been far shorter than the train in the myth.
And the last car had been wide open at the back. As though part of the train had been torn off somewhere along the way.
In other words, that car hadn’t been the ‘original last car.’
I open my eyes and examine the scars on the fragment again.
Monstrous strength enough to tear away an entire section of Surya’s train, which even Cheok Jungyeong or the masters could only break by using their full power.
……This really had to be ‘that.’
Knock, knock, knock.
I looked up at the knock to find Yoo Sangah watching me through a gap in the door.
“I’m sorry, Dokja-ssi. Am I interrupting?”
“Not at all. I’m the one who asked you to come.”
I hurriedly cleared the table and welcomed Yoo Sangah.
She looked around with a slightly uneasy expression before carefully taking the seat across the table from me.
“……Would you like some tea?”
“No, thank you.”
“Then some water……?”
“That would be nice.”
We sat in silence for a while, facing each other across the small table.
I had asked her here, but I didn’t readily broach the subject.
Yoo Sangah would have plenty of questions for me too.
“Go ahead and ask.”
“Actually, I’ve been thinking about you for quite a long time, Dokja-ssi.”
Her tone was almost as though she had been waiting for this.
“Why you know a future no one else knows. How you can stay so calm even in situations like these, and always find answers no one else has thought of.”
“……And have you figured anything out?”
“Some things, I felt I might understand. Others, I couldn’t begin to guess.”
Yoo Sangah had probably studied me.
Just as she studied Spanish on an app in her spare moments, she would have studied me as a person.
And, as always, she would have reached a meaningful conclusion before anyone else.
“Is this world something like a ‘novel’ to you, Dokja-ssi?”
“What made you think that?”
“What you said at the banquet today.”
……That was Yoo Sangah for you.
Really, there was no other way to put it.
―I am a being heading toward the ‘Final Chapter (終章).’
That had been my answer to the question, ‘What is ■■?’ The Final Chapter. The end of all the pages, which you had to reach by turning page after page.
Yoo Sangah continued.
“The constellations were very surprised. Some were shocked, and some were awed.”
The constellations could hardly have reacted otherwise.
That was why I had made the statement in the first place.
“After you left, I asked the Queen of the Underworld why everyone was so surprised.”
“What did she say?”
“She said you were a very special being.”
Yoo Sangah moistened her lips with water and continued.

“I heard that ■■ is given to every being in a ‘different form.’ And I heard that most receive an extremely personal word. I heard that there are countless ■■ in the world, but very few of them are words that suggest an unmistakable ‘end.’”
Something that meant a clear ‘end’ to anyone who heard it.
A word with exceptional universality, applicable to every being.
“She also said that the only beings given a hint of such an unmistakable ‘end’ were great constellations. The highest gods of immense nebulae…… like <Olympus>, <Vedas>, and <Papyrus>.”
“And now…… she said you had become one of them, Dokja-ssi.”
Yoo Sangah looked at me with mixed emotions in her eyes. Her wavering gaze held an emotion that even she herself seemed unable to fully understand.
“That’s a good thing.”
“……A good thing?”
“Because now I can finally start doing something.”
I smiled. Yoo Sangah didn’t.
“After the world fell apart, I thought you seemed happier, Dokja-ssi. You smiled more often than before and seemed more lively…… So I thought it was nice to see. But……”
Her voice trailing off, Yoo Sangah lowered her head.
“Why do you think of this world as ‘fiction,’ Dokja-ssi?”
Yoo Sangah didn’t know me.
What a ‘novel’ was to me.
Exactly what this world meant to me.
I couldn’t explain it, and I mustn’t explain it yet.
“Um, I’m sorry, Dokja-ssi. That was presumptuous of me……”
Even so, Yoo Sangah was the only person who could say something like this to me.
Someone who, alone, noticed what no one else paid any attention to.
[Activating the exclusive skill ‘Character List’!]
She was the first companion I had met.
Perhaps she had been one even before this world began.
[This person’s information cannot be viewed through ‘Character List.’]
Seeing the same message still appear brought an inexplicable sense of relief.
[Information on this person is currently being collected.]
When I had first used ‘Omniscient Reader’s Viewpoint’ on Yoo Sangah, my inability to read her information had made me deeply uneasy.
But for some reason, I now felt the opposite.
I drew a small breath and looked out the window.
A clear sky.
There lay a world where nothing had happened yet.
“There’s something I’d like to ask you to do, Yoo Sangah-ssi.”
That was why now was the only time to prepare.
The nebula <Eden>.

Made up of the angels of the apocalypse, this nebula was the scourge of demonkind and the eternal nemesis of the Demon Realm. Guardians of the heavenly realm, composed of angels who feared no evil (惡) in the world.
Yet even these fearsome angels of <Eden> had something they disliked.
[Therefore, all of you in Eden must adopt the stance of sleeping on your weapons as you await the dawn (枕戈待旦)……]
Metatron’s morning assembly.
And today’s ‘lecturer’ was ‘Jophiel,’ the Commander of the Red Cosmos.
[I urge you never to be taken in by the demons’ two-pronged strategy of peace and war (和戰兩面戰術)……]
Gabriel frowned and tapped the ball of her foot against the ground.
―Ugh, why does it have to be her turn today?
Thousands of lower angels stood in formation on <Eden>’s parade ground. Archangels stood at their head like drill instructors, and Gabriel was one of them.
Lily Blooming in Aquarius, Gabriel.
Guardian of Youths and Travel, Raphael.
Friend of Justice and Harmony, Raguel.
Apart from the archangels away on assignments, most of the constellations of the highest Status who had been lazing around <Eden> had gathered.
Jophiel’s ideological instruction had already been going on for an hour.
Repeatedly stifling yawns, Gabriel swept her drowsy gaze over her colleagues on the parade ground, then suddenly noticed something strange.
―Hey, where’s Uriel?
Raphael, who had been dozing on a cloud, ruffled his curly hair and replied.
―She’s grounded rn.
―Grounded?
―Scribe chewed her out big time. U didn’t know?
―……What did she do?
Looking as though it was a bother, Raphael used the wind to convey his words.
Gabriel’s eyes went round.
―What? Seriously? Uriel?
―Yup yup. Banned from Star Stream broadcasts for 3 years too.
……That Uriel had been sentenced to 3 years of confinement?
The unexpected news brought a grin to Gabriel’s face.
―The Star Stream broadcast boards will be nice and clean for a while.
The morning assembly ended about 30 minutes later.
After dismissing the lower angels, Metatron summoned the archangels separately.

Ash-gray hair reaching down to his waist. Metatron, the ‘Scribe of Heaven,’ looked especially tired today. He had been running himself ragged trying to hold back the sudden surge of probability from ‘Armageddon.’
Pushing up his thin-framed glasses, Metatron spoke.
[Thank you for your work, Jophiel. That was a fine presentation.]
Jophiel bowed her head.
Looking around at the archangels, Metatron asked,
[……Has Uriel not come?]
[I heard you grounded her, Scribe-nim. Like she’d bother showing up.]
The other archangels snickered at Gabriel’s sarcasm.
But Metatron didn’t laugh.

The archangels exchanged glances. There wasn’t an angel here who didn’t know that Uriel was the Scribe’s headache. The first to take the risk of speaking up was the archangel Raguel, whose cheeks bore faint freckles.
[Um, Scribe-nim. Isn’t 3 years of confinement too much? Uriel has become so much brighter lately thanks to the Star Stream broadcasts……]
To constellations who had to endure tedious ages, ‘Star Stream broadcasting’ meant an enormous amount. Some angels even called it the only drug permitted in <Eden>……
[What are you talking about, Raguel? How many times has the Scribe-nim let that ■ off the hook already?]
Raguel’s expression hardened at Gabriel’s words.
[Gabriel. Insulting a fellow angel is a grave offense.]
[Am I wrong? She used to go around chopping off devils’ heads whenever she got bored, then suddenly she got hooked on something weird……]
[Gabriel!]
It was Metatron who calmed the atmosphere before it turned ugly.
[I will decide how Uriel is to be treated.]
At the sublime aura rising around Metatron, all the agitated angels fell silent. Once it was quiet, Metatron turned to the matter at hand.
[I intend to give you a new assignment concerning the Demon Realm Accord.]
The Demon Realm Accord. Tension flickered across the archangels’ faces.
The recent armed conflict in the 73rd Demon Realm had already shaken the balance between <Eden> and the Demon Realm.
[We need an archangel to monitor the ruler of the 73rd Demon Realm, the ‘Demon King of Salvation.’]
At once, bewilderment colored the archangels’ faces.
Gabriel asked in a sharp voice,
[Wait a minute. Wasn’t that originally Uriel’s job? And what does it have to do with the Demon Realm Accord……]
[It is related. And since Uriel is confined, I’m afraid another archangel will have to take on the task.]
Metatron’s gaze swept over the archangels’ faces.
[Raphael begins his doctrinal tour next week, and Raguel is scheduled to visit <Vedas>, so the one without an assignment is……]
The archangels’ gazes, following the Scribe’s, finally came to a stop.
Starting the day after the banquet, the group found themselves enjoying unexpected luxuries.
“……But Dokja-ssi, is it really all right for me to accept something like this?”
“I bought it for you, Hyunsung-ssi.”

As though trying to make up all at once for the time he hadn’t been able to look after his companions, Kim Dokja bought armfuls of things from the [Dokkaebi Bag] every day, dressing his companions in the clothes or using the other items on them. The children were especially excited.
“Hey, look at this, Shin Yoosung!”
“I got one too, you know?”
Draped from head to toe in all kinds of accessories Kim Dokja had bought them, Shin Yoosung and Lee Gilyoung roamed the streets with silly grins. Jung Heewon chuckled at the sight.
“He’s turned the kids into Christmas trees.”
The two squabbling children were sitting on Lee Hyunsung’s broad shoulders. Lee Hyunsung was grinning just as widely. He seemed quite taken with the new shield Kim Dokja had given him.
“……Three idiots.”
Muttering that, she glanced to the side and saw Lee Jihye approaching with a beaming smile, wearing a helmet shaped like a triangular gimbap.
If those three were Christmas trees, this one was a three-tier cake.
“Hasn’t Dokja ajusshi been really nice to us lately?”
“Maybe he’s finally realized how precious his companions are.”
At Jung Heewon’s response, Lee Jihye narrowed her eyes and said, “Hmm.”
“Unnie…… Don’t tell me you didn’t get anything?”
“I don’t need anything, okay?”
In fact, Kim Dokja had visited Jung Heewon several times too.
But there had been no items, only information about a few hidden pieces and instruction in training methods.
She could still vividly recall Kim Dokja’s oddly dejected face as he left after she retorted that she could manage on her own now without him telling her those things.
She was about to rap the snickering Lee Jihye on the head when someone poked her shoulder.
Turning around, she found Kim Dokja, who looked rather tired.
“Oh, Dokja-ssi……”
With deep dark circles under his eyes, Kim Dokja held something out to Jung Heewon.
“This is……”
“A new suit. You’ll find it easier to move in.”
Jung Heewon accepted the clothes before she quite knew what she was doing.
It was a blue-black commando uniform with a large cape attached. She had seen it at the exchange once, but had given up on it because it was too expensive.
“This is far too expensive. What I have now is more than enough……”
Kim Dokja silently shook his head. Looking at his unreadable expression brought back an old memory. Come to think of it, he had given her clothes like this back in their Chungmuro days too.
They’d been rags back then……
[The constellation ‘Bald General of Justice’ feels hurt by the incarnation ‘Jung Heewon.’]
“You promised to be my sword, didn’t you? This is the least I can do.”

Leaving her with those words, Kim Dokja was already far away, apparently with something else to do. Watching his retreating back, Jung Heewon stroked the commando uniform left in her hands. Beside her, Lee Jihye teased,
“Unnie, your mouth……”
“What?”
“Nothing, there’s just something at the corners of your mouth. Anyway, unnie, if you don’t like it, trade it for my admiral’s helmet. I’ve always dreamed of wearing a commando uniform.”
“No.”

Looking closely, she found an emblem on the uniform similar to the one on Lee Hyunsung’s shield. Mah-deh bah-ee…… Yahn-guh…… saen……? Not being fluent in English, Jung Heewon scratched her head and gave up trying to read it. Anyway, it had to be good.
“But why is that guy suddenly acting like this? I heard he even charged people for food……”
“Who knows. Maybe he’s cooking up another weird scheme, like before.”
It certainly wouldn’t be strange for Kim Dokja.
Having given them such good items, he would surely work them to the bone again.

Feeling like an office worker who had received an advance on her salary, Jung Heewon tried draping the uniform’s coat this way and that. As she and Lee Jihye discussed how to wear it to look even cooler, someone appeared like a ghost and trudged past them.
“Sangah-ssi, is something wrong?”
“Pardon? Oh, yes. No.”
Yoo Sangah, who had been staring blankly into space, started and opened and closed her mouth. Empty eyes. Realizing something was wrong, Jung Heewon was about to speak, but Lee Jihye beat her to it.
“Aha, I get it. You didn’t get an item either, Sangah unnie?”
Jung Heewon jabbed her in the side, and Lee Jihye doubled over with a small squeal. Yoo Sangah smiled weakly.
“I suppose I’ve just had a lot on my mind lately. ……Anyway, that outfit looks wonderful, Heewon-ssi.”
“Oh, yes. Dokja-ssi gave it to me…… Though now that I’ve tried it on, I’m wondering if it’s a bit much.”
“I think it suits you.”
“You do? Thank you.”
Embarrassed, Jung Heewon scratched her head.
A bracelet she hadn’t seen before gleamed on Yoo Sangah’s wrist.
Just as things were about to get awkward, Jung Heewon saw an opening.
“By the way, how are things with Dokja-ssi these days?”
“……Dokja-ssi?”
Yoo Sangah’s face as she repeated the question, as though she had no idea what Jung Heewon meant.
Wondering if she had gotten the wrong idea, Jung Heewon stumbled over her words.
“Um, uh, I mean…… I was just wondering if you two were getting along……”
Tilting her head, Yoo Sangah touched her lips and murmured,
“Hmm, I think it’s about the same as when we worked at the company……”
About the same as when they worked at the company. Judging by that response, the prospects didn’t look very promising. Lee Jihye whispered to Jung Heewon.
“I told you before. There’s nothing between them. Dokja ajusshi’s tastes don’t run that way, they run toward our……”
“……Now I see why my sponsor likes you. Has that precious master of yours woken up?”
“Not yet. They said it would take a few more days.”
Far away, Kim Dokja was limply making his way toward the ward like a squid, unaware that they were talking about him.
“Maybe he’s going to give him something too……”

The sun was slowly sinking beyond the nearly completed clock tower. The group’s boisterous laughter rang out. Gong Pildu could be seen taking apart something like a machine gun, while Han Myungoh tested his new prosthetic leg in various ways.
For some reason, Jung Heewon’s heart swelled.
They were all together now.

Soon they would return to Earth and plunge once more into the hell of the scenarios. Even so, Jung Heewon wasn’t afraid. Watching the sun set behind the clock tower, she recalled something she had heard in the Theatre Dungeon.
―I wished to see the epilogue of a certain novel.
Kim Dokja had looked so lonely when he said that.
Back then, she hadn’t even understood what he meant, but now she felt she might understand a little. And there was at least one thing she knew for certain.
When that ‘epilogue’ came, Kim Dokja would not be alone.

Several days after the banquet. The constellations staying in the [Industrial Complex] began to leave one by one. I was about to go outside to see them off when I found two flowers tucked into my coat’s breast pocket.
“What are these?”
A pair: a red cosmos and a lily.
Quite a mismatched combination. ……Was this the kids’ doing?

For now, I took the flowers with me and went out to the square. Several constellations were already passing through the portal. Some of those leaving had signed special contracts with the nebula <Kim Dokja’s Company>, and the old man in front of me was one of them.
[You look like a man preparing for war. There should be no need to rush quite so much.]
“Scenarios are always war.”
The ‘Mass Production Maker’ laughed heartily at my reply.
[Don’t grow numb to it. I hope you’ll become someone different from the other constellations.]
“Thank you for your help.”
I smiled as well and bowed my head. Opening the door of his vehicle, the ‘Mass Production Maker’ paused and looked back at me.
[There’s one last thing I’d like to ask……]
“Of course. Ask anything you like.”
But the Mass Production Maker didn’t ask his question right away.
Instead, he took a cigarette from inside his clothes and worked it between his lips.
[……Have you ever thought about what ■■ actually is?]
The lighter clicked, and the tip of the cigarette caught fire.
Exhaling smoke like a sigh, the Mass Production Maker continued.
[Is it somewhere we reach because we want to, or somewhere fate makes us reach? Is it a place, a life, or perhaps a particular time and space?]
The ‘Mass Production Maker’ had probably turned those questions over countless times.
And in the end, he probably hadn’t found an answer.
“What’s certain is that it’s where every story ends.”
[Sometimes I find your composure quite remarkable.]
“I get nervous too.”
[I’ve thought this since the Gourmet Association, but you’re worse at lying than I expected.]
The Mass Production Maker smiled like a child.
[Which is why I ask…… Is your ■■ really the ‘Final Chapter’?]
A question that caught me off guard.
I reflexively parted my lips, then closed them again.
The ‘Mass Production Maker’ waited patiently for my answer. I only spoke after the cigarette in his hand had burned down by about half.
“I don’t know where the story will take me. But…… I’m certain that the Final Chapter is where I want to go.”
Even after I finished speaking, he continued to listen.
As though my story were still going on.
Only after the remaining half of his cigarette had burned away did the ‘Mass Production Maker’ smile.
[I hope I’m on your last page too.]
“Have a safe journey, sir.”
[Take care of yourself.]

With a soft hum of its engine, the ‘Mass Production Maker’s’ vehicle slid into the portal. The other constellations disappeared through it one by one. As the portal closed, ominous sparks writhed on the far side of the empty sky.
Watching those sparks, I gently stroked the flower petals in my pocket.
About three days remained.
Soon, this [Industrial Complex]’s most important story would begin.
